articles.title: Asian stocks mixed as yen jumps against dollar, while oil prices fall
articles.excerpt:
Asian shares were mixed Monday after the US and Japan confirmed they had acted to prop up the value of the Japanese yen against the US dollar, causing the yen to rise to its highest level since late last year.

Oil prices fell sharply after US President Donald Trump said he would order US forces to refrain from attacks against Iran, claiming a deal to end the fighting in the Middle East was close.

The dollar fell as low as 155.20 against the yen after Trump and Japanese officials confirmed they had intervened last week to curb the US currency's rise to 40-year highs against the yen. Last week it was trading near 164 yen.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan stocks slide as stronger Yen hits exporters; Nikkei drops Over 2%
articles.excerpt:
Japanese stocks tumbled as a sharp rally in the yen weighed on export-oriented companies, with the Nikkei falling over 2%. Auto and chip stocks led the declines, although SoftBank, Lasertec and Kioxia outperformed. Investors are now watching for further currency intervention and its impact on corporate earnings and market sentiment.

articles.title: Yen Rises Amid Speculation of More Intervention After US Support
articles.excerpt:
The yen rallied sharply on Monday amid speculation that authorities may have intervened to prop up the currency again after coordinated action between the US and Japan last week.

The yen swung from a small decline to gain as much as 1.4% versus the dollar during morning trading in Tokyo. It then pared a large chunk of the move in a choppy market, raising the prospect that jittery traders or algorithms may also have been the cause. It was quoted around 156.30 as of 11:37 a.m. local time.

articles.title: US stock market today: Wall Street futures gain as easing Iran tensions trigger sharp fall in oil prices
articles.excerpt:
US stock futures traded higher on Monday, 3 August, as investor risk appetite improved after US President Donald Trump called off a planned military strike on Iran, triggering a sharp decline in crude oil prices and easing concerns over a broader conflict in the Middle East.

Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 413 points, or 0.8%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.6% and Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.4%. Monday also marks the first trading session of August, with Wall Street looking to stabilise after a volatile July.

articles.title: Indian Oil Subsidiary CPCL Plans 280,000 Bpd Manali Refinery
articles.excerpt:

President Volodymyr Zelensky secured new…

Indian refiner Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited plans to boost the crude oil refining capacity at its Manali refinery by a third to 280,000 barrels per day (bpd), the refiner said in its 2025/2026 report.

Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) is a subsidiary of the country's top state-controlled refiner, Indian Oil Corporation. The refinery at Manali, Chennai, has facilities to produce fuels, lubricants, waxes, and petrochemicals.

The current capacity of 210,000 bpd will be increased to 280,000 bpd under CPCL's plan, which did not give a timeline for the expansion.
